newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech cbank sets two rev repos to drain funds.
newsitem.headline: Czech cbank sets two rev repos to drain funds.

text.p: The Czech National Bank (CNB) on Wednesday set a one-week reverse repo tender to drain funds from the market at a maximum rate of 31 percent, down from 39 percent in a similar operation on Monday.
The CNB also set a two week reverse repo tender at a maximum of 29 percent, down from 39 percent.
The CNB said it would accept two bids from participants of a minimum 100 million crowns until 10.15 a.m. (0815 GMT) in the two-week operation.
Similar restrictions were placed on bids for the one-week tender, which must be placed by 10.30 a.m. (0830 GMT).
The central bank has been holding several tenders on almost a daily basis in the past weeks in order to drain liquidity from the market and help support the crown.

The CNB has restricted banks from access to Lombard credit, after raising it to 50 percent from 14 percent. It has also limited foreign banks' access to the money market and raised its discount rate to 13 percent from 10.5 percent.
